tasks.behavior: Guide merchants through supported setup tasks
acceptance: Merchant and developer setup guides sharing a link, billing a customer or integrating checkout using actual billing/store/branding/acceptance/key/origin/webhook state.
The existing first store is reused; completion survives reload through actual resources and respects role permissions.
KYB honestly remains not_required and never blocks test keys or invoices; obsolete API-later messaging is removed.
Onboarding starts only after all other phase 11 features and their checks are complete, including integration, held-money refunds and history.

tasks.behavior: Implement hosted and origin-restricted embedded checkout
acceptance: Hosted integration works without a browser package; full and element embeds reuse trusted checkout and support existing payment lifecycles.
Only configured exact origins can frame an embed; normal pay pages remain unframeable; loopback HTTP is test-only and live returns require HTTPS.
Message origin/source checks, strict CSP, revocation, expiration and forged parent/redirect events are tested; browser hints never prove fulfillment.

tasks.behavior: Build minimal JavaScript and React checkout packages
acceptance: Browser packages provide PayButton, Checkout and PaymentElement over existing checkout URLs, without secret keys or client-authoritative financial state.
Typed messages verify origin/source and mount lifecycle cleans listeners; React 18 and 19 compatibility, type/build/size and packed-install checks pass.
Release artifacts, changelogs and provenance CI are prepared; publishing remains gated by separate approval.

tasks.behavior: Prove merchant checkout fulfillment and reconciliation end to end
acceptance: The example merchant prices a cart on its server, creates real checkouts, verifies events and fulfills an order once across hosted and embedded flows.
Independent shared-link customers, client invoicing, multi-store isolation, expiration, partial payment, delivery recovery and spoofed prices/messages have automated workflow coverage.
Ledger/export totals reconcile against receiver and wallet chain balances; duplicate/reordered events cannot double-fulfill.
Quickstart and integration docs match implemented packages; provider limitations, actual user testing and release approvals are reported truthfully.

tasks.behavior: The links list pages by cursor with bounded reads
acceptance: GET links reads one page at a time with a limit and a cursor, and the links list loads the next page on demand

tasks.behavior: Client and store pages read only their own record
acceptance: The client and store pages read their record by id and never load the whole list to show it

tasks.behavior: The balance chart and its totals value tokens at the market prices the total uses
acceptance: The balance chart, its change figure and the received and sent totals value tokens at the same market prices as the total beside them, or R-178 records why they count each stablecoin as 1 USD
notes: 2026-10-30 Narrowed: the invoice page part (R-54, R-55, R-69) shipped in F397.

tasks.behavior: The overview's Received and My assets cards keep their size while they load
acceptance: On a phone the Received card's range control keeps its line when the transfer count arrives, and My assets keeps its height from loading to loaded

tasks.behavior: A payer claims held money from the pay page
acceptance: A payer with held money presses Claim refund on /pay, connects the wallet that sent it and signs a claim naming the invoice and the destination; plain and smart-contract wallet signatures are both verified
An exchange deposit gives a destination and support evidence instead of a signature (Q-9)
Claims live in refund_claims with states the payer sees, and each state change reaches the payer receipt email once
From an embed, Claim refund opens the hosted page in a new tab

tasks.behavior: The owner sees money sent above the amount and can return it
acceptance: The owner's invoice page shows money sent above the amount as held for the payer, with a way to return it through the refund flow

tasks.behavior: An ops command approves refund claims and prints the Safe refund call
acceptance: cmd/ops lists claims and approves or rejects each with a reason; approval sets the invoice's refund status to refund_pending before the Safe call is queued
It prints the refund(to, amount) call for the refund-authority Safe, one refund of everything held by default, with no new hot key
The watcher books the refund once, and it shows on the payment page beside the payments and the settlement

tasks.behavior: A payer who sent on the wrong network can open a recovery claim
acceptance: The payer gives a transaction hash; the API finds it on an enabled chain and opens a recovery claim; recover() is offered only where our factory exists, and no page promises recovery

tasks.behavior: Held-money refunds pass end to end on Anvil
acceptance: On Anvil: overpay, expired partial and late payments each go claim then refund, a smart-wallet claim passes, and the ledger matches the chain after each
